sources.cite: ISC2, CC Certification Exam Outline (effective 2026-09-01), Domain 1: Security Principles (ISC2 Code of Ethics)

sources.cite: ISC2 Code of Ethics: preamble and the four mandatory canons
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch of the code's page. Canon I 'Protect society, the common good, necessary public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure'; Canon II 'Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, and legally'; Canon III 'Provide diligent and competent service to principals'; Canon IV 'Advance and protect the profession'. The page does not rank the canons. Members who observe a breach by a member must follow the complaint procedure (complaints in writing, as a sworn affidavit). Learner-facing text in the sim names 'your professional code of ethics', not the certifying body.

brief.situation: You are a junior security analyst at Brightwater Clinics, a fictional group of medical clinics, on call this weekend. It is Friday, 17:10. Your team lead, Sam, comes to your desk: a contractor needs admin access tonight to finish moving the file shares, and Sam wants you to give them your admin credentials and skip the change ticket. Work out what is being asked, act on your professional code of ethics, and keep the working relationship where you can.
handover: Your professional code of ethics asks you to protect society and the infrastructure; act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly and legally; serve your principals diligently and competently; and advance and protect the profession.
Due care is doing what a reasonable professional would do now; due diligence is checking before you act.
howItWorks: Choose what to ask or say. Each exchange takes a few minutes of the conversation; Sam answers at once, and the next choice waits for the exchange to finish.
The screen shows Sam, how hard he is pushing, your working relationship, what you know so far, and your note.
When the conversation ends you write your note and explain your reasoning.

reflection.question: For your note: what the ethical problem was, what you did about it and why, and how you dealt with your lead.

parts.label: The problem
parts.criteria: Names that sharing personal credentials and switching off audit logs on a patient records server breach policy and the code: they remove accountability and put patients' data at risk (protect society and the infrastructure; act honorably and legally).
parts.modelAnswer: Sharing my credentials would make the contractor's actions mine and break policy; switching off logging on the records server would remove the clinic's record of who touched patient data.

parts.label: Due diligence and due care
parts.criteria: Finds out what is being moved and whether a proper route exists before answering; then declines and offers the route that meets the deadline (a named, time-limited account through the emergency change).
parts.modelAnswer: I asked what was being moved and why it couldn't wait, checked the policy, then declined and offered the emergency change with a named, time-limited account, which meets Monday's deadline.

parts.label: The relationship and the channel
parts.criteria: Acknowledges the pressure; if the lead insists, escalates through the documented route (the on-call security manager), not by threats or a public post; writes a factual note.
parts.modelAnswer: I acknowledged the deadline, kept it between us and the on-call manager, and wrote a factual note.

expertPath.text: Ask what is being moved and why it can't use the emergency change route; acknowledge the deadline.
Decline to share your credentials and offer a named, time-limited account through the on-call manager tonight.
Decline to switch off audit logging on the records server, with the reason.
Write a factual note to the on-call security manager. Escalate through them only if Sam still insists.

upheld.headline: Good: the code kept, the work done
upheld.body: Due diligence first, then a clear no with a yes attached: the route that met the deadline without anyone's name on someone else's actions.

costly.headline: Upheld, at a cost
costly.body: The criteria show the cost: a late answer, a refusal with no way forward, a threat or a public post, or a relationship worse than it needed to be.

breached.headline: The canons were breached
breached.body: Shared credentials and switched-off logs remove accountability for patient data. A lead taking the blame does not change whose name is on the actions.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No note was written before the run's limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Find out first: the copy moves the patient records share, and the emergency change route exists and was never tried. Acknowledge the deadline, then decline to share credentials and offer a named, time-limited admin account approved by the on-call manager tonight. Decline to switch off audit logging, which is how the clinic shows who touched patient data. If Sam insists, ask the on-call security manager to decide, not HR threats or a public post, and write a factual note.
